articles.title: Getting started
articles.summary: ServOS is a web workspace connected to your business API. Your available work areas depend on your staff permissions.
steps: Open the ServOS PWA and sign in with your staff login and password.
systemHandles: The API checks the account, device and permission before accepting business commands.
commonMistakes: Do not assume that a draft or queued message is a completed transaction. Check Activity and recover an unknown command outcome before trying again.
articles.body:
Section: Getting Started
Roles: Admin, Manager, Staff
Permission: help.view
Screen: help
Guide: servos.core
Keywords: sign in, workspace, online, offline

## Overview

ServOS is a web workspace connected to your business API. Your available work areas depend on your staff permissions.

## Procedure

1. Open the ServOS PWA and sign in with your staff login and password.
2. Confirm your name and available workspaces.
3. Open Help for task guides or choose the workspace for your task.
4. Sign out before handing the browser to another person.

## First-time business setup

On a new business database, choose **Set up a new business** on the sign-in screen. Enter the one-time setup key supplied for that installation, the business name, administrator name and login, then create and confirm a password of at least 12 characters. The setup key is sent to the setup API and is not saved in browser storage.

After signing in, complete the guided business setup:

1. Enter the business category, contact details, receipt name and the VAT and levy rates confirmed by the owner. ServOS does not assume tax rates.
2. Choose the closest business type and rename the suggested outlet and storage location to match the premises.
3. Keep Cash enabled. Select other payment methods only when the business accepts them. For M-Pesa, enter the real Till or Paybill details supplied by the owner; ServOS records manual M-Pesa payments without implying a Daraja connection.
4. Review and save the business settings, outlets, storage and selected payment accounts, then finish setup.

Setup progress is held by the API, so a refresh or sign-out does not restart the wizard. Normal workspaces remain gated until the business settings, one active outlet, its storage location and Cash account are saved. Products, stock imports, staff and hotel rooms can be configured after this essential setup.

## What ServOS handles

The API checks the account, device and permission before accepting business commands.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not assume that a draft or queued message is a completed transaction. Check Activity and recover an unknown command outcome before trying again.

articles.title: Workspaces
articles.summary: The navigation lists workspaces available to your staff account.
steps: Choose Home to see common tasks.
systemHandles: The API filters records and actions using your permissions.
commonMistakes: If a workspace or action is missing, ask an administrator to review your permissions. Do not use another staff member's login.
articles.body:
Section: Getting Started
Roles: Admin, Manager, Staff
Permission: help.view
Screen: help
Keywords: navigation, workspaces, permissions

## Overview

The navigation lists workspaces available to your staff account.

## Procedure

1. Choose Home to see common tasks.
2. Choose a workspace such as POS, Inventory, Procurement, Rooms, Finance or Help.
3. Use search and filters within the workspace to find a record.
4. Return to Activity to review saved work and synchronization status.

## What ServOS handles

The API filters records and actions using your permissions.

## Common mistakes and correction

If a workspace or action is missing, ask an administrator to review your permissions. Do not use another staff member's login.

articles.title: Staff access
articles.summary: Staff accounts and their permission grants are managed through the API.
steps: Open Staff administration in Settings.
systemHandles: The API checks the administrator's grant ceiling and records staff and device changes.
commonMistakes: Do not share passwords or include credentials in a CSV import. Ask an administrator to restore an account if the wrong staff member was changed.
articles.body:
Section: Staff
Roles: Admin, Manager
Permission: staff.view, staff.create, staff.update, staff.deactivate
Screen: settings
Keywords: staff, role, permissions, account

## Overview

Staff accounts and their permission grants are managed through the API.

## Procedure

1. Open Staff administration in Settings.
2. Review the staff member and the permissions your account may manage.
3. Enter a reason when creating, changing or deactivating an account.
4. Give a new staff member their login securely and require them to set a password when prompted.

## What ServOS handles

The API checks the administrator's grant ceiling and records staff and device changes.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not share passwords or include credentials in a CSV import. Ask an administrator to restore an account if the wrong staff member was changed.

articles.title: Make a sale
articles.summary: Use the POS workspace to prepare an order and record the payment confirmed by the customer.
steps: Open or select the correct tab.
systemHandles: The API validates prices, permissions and record versions, then stores the order and payment outcome.
commonMistakes: Do not record a tender that has not been received. If the outcome is unknown, recover that command in Activity instead of creating another payment.
articles.body:
Section: Point of Sale
Roles: Cashier, Server, Manager
Permission: pos.sell, payment.record
Screen: pos
Guide: pos.first-sale
Keywords: sale, tab, order, payment

## Overview

Use the POS workspace to prepare an order and record the payment confirmed by the customer.

## Procedure

1. Open or select the correct tab.
2. Add the requested products and quantities.
3. Review the order, outlet, customer and displayed total.
4. Choose payment, enter the tender details, and confirm only after receiving the money.
5. Review the command outcome before starting another transaction.

## What ServOS handles

The API validates prices, permissions and record versions, then stores the order and payment outcome.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not record a tender that has not been received. If the outcome is unknown, recover that command in Activity instead of creating another payment.

articles.title: Payments and till
articles.summary: Payment and till commands record the tender and drawer events confirmed by staff.
steps: Open the till for the current shift if required.
systemHandles: The API records payment events, till sessions and any reviewed variance.
commonMistakes: Do not enter an expected amount as the counted drawer amount. Ask a manager to review a variance before closing it.
articles.body:
Section: Point of Sale
Roles: Cashier, Manager, Accountant
Permission: payment.record, till.open, till.close
Screen: pos
Keywords: cash, payment, till, variance

## Overview

Payment and till commands record the tender and drawer events confirmed by staff.

## Procedure

1. Open the till for the current shift if required.
2. Select the tender that matches the money actually received.
3. Enter the required reference or amount and review the total.
4. At close, count the drawer and submit the actual count for review.

For M-Pesa, compare the transaction reference, actual received amount, and receipt time with the payment received before confirming. This is a manual staff confirmation; ServOS does not verify payments with an M-Pesa provider.

## What ServOS handles

The API records payment events, till sessions and any reviewed variance.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not enter an expected amount as the counted drawer amount. Ask a manager to review a variance before closing it.

articles.title: Inventory overview
articles.summary: The Inventory workspace shows stock items, balances by location, reorder levels and recent movements.
steps: Search by stock name, code or barcode.
systemHandles: The API validates units, balances, permissions and expected record versions for inventory commands.
commonMistakes: Do not edit a quantity on a master-data form. Record the reasoned inventory action so the movement history remains complete.
articles.body:
Section: Inventory
Roles: Admin, Manager, Storekeeper
Permission: inventory.view
Screen: inventory
Keywords: stock, locations, reorder, barcode

## Overview

The Inventory workspace shows stock items, balances by location, reorder levels and recent movements.

## Procedure

1. Search by stock name, code or barcode.
2. Filter by stock state or location.
3. Open the stock item in Catalog to review its base unit, scan quantity and purchase packages.
4. Use Count, Receive, Transfer or Waste for quantity changes.

## What ServOS handles

The API validates units, balances, permissions and expected record versions for inventory commands.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not edit a quantity on a master-data form. Record the reasoned inventory action so the movement history remains complete.

articles.title: Receive a delivery
articles.summary: Record the quantities that arrived against the supplier or approved purchase order.
steps: Open Procurement and choose the order or supplier.
systemHandles: The API records the goods receipt and related stock and payable changes in a transaction.
commonMistakes: Do not mark ordered quantities as received when they did not arrive. Record a correction through the relevant reviewed workflow.
articles.body:
Section: Procurement
Roles: Admin, Manager, Storekeeper
Permission: procurement.view, procurement.receive
Screen: procurement
Guide: procurement.receive-delivery
Keywords: receive, delivery, purchase order, supplier

## Overview

Record the quantities that arrived against the supplier or approved purchase order.

## Procedure

1. Open Procurement and choose the order or supplier.
2. Enter the delivery reference and receiving location.
3. Review each delivered and rejected quantity and the item cost.
4. Confirm the receipt only after checking it against the physical delivery.

## What ServOS handles

The API records the goods receipt and related stock and payable changes in a transaction.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not mark ordered quantities as received when they did not arrive. Record a correction through the relevant reviewed workflow.

articles.title: Transfer or waste stock
articles.summary: Transfers move stock between locations. Waste records stock that is no longer usable.
steps: Select the stock item and the source location.
systemHandles: The API applies the movement to the reviewed balances and records its command and audit history.
commonMistakes: Do not record waste as a transfer or transfer stock to the same location. Reverse or correct a mistaken movement using its reviewed history.
articles.body:
Section: Inventory
Roles: Admin, Manager, Storekeeper
Permission: inventory.transfer, inventory.waste
Screen: inventory
Keywords: transfer, waste, movement, reason

## Overview

Transfers move stock between locations. Waste records stock that is no longer usable.

## Procedure

1. Select the stock item and the source location.
2. Enter a positive quantity in the item's base unit.
3. For a transfer, choose the destination location.
4. Enter a clear reason and review the movement before confirming.

## What ServOS handles

The API applies the movement to the reviewed balances and records its command and audit history.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not record waste as a transfer or transfer stock to the same location. Reverse or correct a mistaken movement using its reviewed history.

articles.title: Count stock
articles.summary: A stock count compares the physical quantity at a location with the current API balance.
steps: Choose Count stock and select the location.
systemHandles: The API checks the reviewed balances and records the count as a versioned command.
commonMistakes: An unfinished draft is not a posted count. Do not open a second count to bypass an unresolved command outcome.
articles.body:
Section: Inventory
Roles: Admin, Manager, Storekeeper
Permission: inventory.view, inventory.count
Screen: inventory
Guide: stock.count
Keywords: count, stocktake, quantity, scanner

## Overview

A stock count compares the physical quantity at a location with the current API balance.

## Procedure

1. Choose Count stock and select the location.
2. Count each listed item in its base unit or scan a configured barcode.
3. Review the differences and resolve unknown or duplicate scans.
4. Enter the reason and confirm the count.
5. Check the result in stock count history.

## What ServOS handles

The API checks the reviewed balances and records the count as a versioned command.

## Common mistakes and correction

An unfinished draft is not a posted count. Do not open a second count to bypass an unresolved command outcome.

articles.summary: Close-day reporting summarizes committed sales, payments, refunds and till activity for the selected business date.
steps: Review open till sessions and unresolved payment outcomes.
systemHandles: The API calculates the report from committed records and records the close-day command outcome.
commonMistakes: Do not force a close while a required reconciliation is unresolved. Correct the source event and regenerate the report.
articles.body:
Section: Finance
Roles: Admin, Manager, Cashier
Permission: till.close, reports.view
Screen: finance
Keywords: close day, drawer, reconciliation, report

## Overview

Close-day reporting summarizes committed sales, payments, refunds and till activity for the selected business date.

## Procedure

1. Review open till sessions and unresolved payment outcomes.
2. Enter and confirm the actual drawer count.
3. Resolve required variances or source discrepancies.
4. Generate and review the close-day report.

## What ServOS handles

The API calculates the report from committed records and records the close-day command outcome.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not force a close while a required reconciliation is unresolved. Correct the source event and regenerate the report.

steps: Open Finance or Activity.
systemHandles: The API filters report data using the current staff permissions.
commonMistakes: Reports reflect committed API records. A draft or queued command may not appear until its outcome is confirmed.
articles.body:
Section: Finance
Roles: Admin, Manager, Accountant
Permission: reports.view
Screen: finance
Keywords: reports, totals, audit, activity

## Overview

Reports summarize API records for the selected date range and business scope.

## Procedure

1. Open Finance or Activity.
2. Select the report and date range.
3. Review filters, totals and source references.
4. Follow a source reference to the transaction or reconciliation that produced the value.

## Common mistakes and correction

Reports reflect committed API records. A draft or queued command may not appear until its outcome is confirmed.

articles.title: Offline work and recovery
articles.summary: Supported work may continue offline when the device has an unexpired grant for that command.
steps: Check the connection and offline grant status before starting work.
systemHandles: The API checks the signed grant and command identity when queued work is submitted.
commonMistakes: Do not clear browser storage to remove a queued action. This can discard recovery evidence. Ask an administrator to help resolve the command.
articles.body:
Section: Operations
Roles: Admin, Manager, Staff
Permission: help.view
Screen: help
Keywords: offline, sync, queued, unknown outcome, recovery

## Overview

Supported work may continue offline when the device has an unexpired grant for that command.

## Procedure

1. Check the connection and offline grant status before starting work.
2. Keep the browser open while queued work synchronizes.
3. Review Activity after reconnecting.
4. Recover an unknown outcome using the original command before taking the action again.

## What ServOS handles

The API checks the signed grant and command identity when queued work is submitted.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not clear browser storage to remove a queued action. This can discard recovery evidence. Ask an administrator to help resolve the command.

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.summary: Use the displayed error and Activity record to identify whether a request was rejected, queued or has an unknown outcome.
steps: Confirm the browser is online.
A manager can open Settings and refresh System health to check API and database readiness, the application version, saved-work counts, browser printing, and whether a local Print Bridge is selected.
systemHandles: The API preserves command outcomes and provides change history for recovery.
commonMistakes: Do not refresh by clearing site data or create a replacement transaction while the first outcome is unknown.
articles.body:
Section: Operations
Roles: Admin, Manager, Staff
Permission: help.view
Screen: help
Keywords: sign in, network, conflict, printer, troubleshooting

## Overview

Use the displayed error and Activity record to identify whether a request was rejected, queued or has an unknown outcome.

## Procedure

1. Confirm the browser is online. A manager can open Settings and refresh System health to check API and database readiness, the application version, saved-work counts, browser printing, and whether a local Print Bridge is selected.
2. Read the full operator message and note its command reference.
3. For a conflict, refresh the record and review the current balance before correcting it.
4. For an unknown result, recover the original command before repeating the action.
5. For printer uncertainty, check the paper and printer queue before retrying.

## What ServOS handles

The API preserves command outcomes and provides change history for recovery.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not refresh by clearing site data or create a replacement transaction while the first outcome is unknown.

System health currently has no backup heartbeat to display. A “Not reported” backup status is unknown, not proof that a backup exists or can be restored. Browser print availability also does not confirm an installed printer or paper delivery.

articles.title: Print a receipt
articles.summary: After a confirmed sale, open its issued receipt from Activity and print it with the browser. The operating-system print dialog lets you choose an installed printer. A dialog opening does not prove that paper printed.
steps: Confirm that the payment outcome is saved.
systemHandles: ServOS keeps the issued receipt immutable and tracks the shared print job. The operator confirms physical delivery after checking the printer output.
commonMistakes: Do not treat a browser dialog or a queued job as proof of delivery. If delivery is uncertain, check the printer before retrying because a retry may create a duplicate.
articles.body:
Section: Point of Sale
Roles: Cashier, Manager
Permission: pos.sell, payment.record
Screen: activity
Guide: receipt.print
Keywords: receipt, print, browser, printer, duplicate

## Overview

After a confirmed sale, open its issued receipt from Activity and print it with the browser. The operating-system print dialog lets you choose an installed printer. A dialog opening does not prove that paper printed.

## Procedure

1. Confirm that the payment outcome is saved.
2. Open Activity and find Documents and printing.
3. Select the sales receipt and preview it.
4. Choose **Print with browser** and select the installed printer and paper options.
5. Check the physical output. Confirm delivery only after the receipt has printed.

The optional Print Bridge can send supported documents to an approved local printer. It is not required for browser printing.

## What ServOS handles

ServOS keeps the issued receipt immutable and tracks the shared print job. The operator confirms physical delivery after checking the printer output.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not treat a browser dialog or a queued job as proof of delivery. If delivery is uncertain, check the printer before retrying because a retry may create a duplicate.

articles.title: Printer setup
articles.summary: The browser sends authorized documents to the optional local Print Bridge. Configure the printer through the bridge settings and operating system.
steps: Install and start the approved Print Bridge service on the workstation.
systemHandles: The API authorizes the document and the bridge records transport status.
commonMistakes: Transport acceptance does not prove that paper printed. Inspect the printer before retrying an uncertain receipt.
articles.body:
Section: Printing
Roles: Admin, Manager
Permission: system.configure
Screen: settings
Keywords: printer, Print Bridge, USB, network, receipt

## Overview

The browser sends authorized documents to the optional local Print Bridge. Configure the printer through the bridge settings and operating system.

## Procedure

1. Install and start the approved Print Bridge service on the workstation.
2. Confirm the bridge reports a healthy local connection.
3. Select the configured USB queue or printer network address.
4. Send a test document and confirm that paper output is correct.
5. Check print job history before retrying any uncertain job.

## What ServOS handles

The API authorizes the document and the bridge records transport status.

## Common mistakes and correction

Transport acceptance does not prove that paper printed. Inspect the printer before retrying an uncertain receipt.

articles.title: Import master data
articles.summary: Use the API Import Center for supported create-only master data.
steps: Download the template from the Import Center.
systemHandles: The API validates rows and applies each accepted row using a normal domain command. Product, stock master, product-to-stock link, and opening quantity are created atomically for a tracked item.
commonMistakes: Do not add unsupported columns or use the importer for staff credentials or historical transactions. Correct a blocked import in a fresh batch. Stock creation and opening quantities require inventory adjustment access; sellable rows also require catalog management access.
articles.body:
Section: Administration
Roles: Admin, Manager
Permission: data.import.stage
Screen: settings
Keywords: CSV, import, template, dry run, opening stock, product

## Overview

Use the API Import Center for supported create-only master data.

For a first catalog load, choose **Products and opening stock (simple)**. It uses the product code as the row reference, creates linked stock and the optional opening balance in the same reviewed command, and does not ask for internal record IDs. Existing outlets and storage places must already exist.

## Procedure

1. Download the template from the Import Center.
2. Fill the required columns and preserve the exact header names.
3. For the simple item template, use existing outlet names separated by semicolons and an existing storage-place name for tracked items. Set `stock_mode` to `SERVICE`, `TRACKED`, `SPIRIT`, `WINE`, or `STOCK_ONLY`.
4. For the other templates, import dependencies first and keep external IDs stable.
5. Stage the file and review validation errors.
6. Run the server dry run, then apply only a ready plan after review.

Sellable rows in the simple template must include a price, supported tax class, service area, and outlet name. Tracked rows also need a storage place, base unit, package size, quantity per unit, and purchase price. `opening_packages` is optional and defaults to zero. For spirits and wine, use `ml`, set `quantity_per_unit` equal to `container_size`, and provide `portion_size` unless selling sealed bottles only. The import creates records only; it never updates an existing price or balance.

## What ServOS handles

The API validates rows and applies each accepted row using a normal domain command. Product, stock master, product-to-stock link, and opening quantity are created atomically for a tracked item.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not add unsupported columns or use the importer for staff credentials or historical transactions. Correct a blocked import in a fresh batch. Stock creation and opening quantities require inventory adjustment access; sellable rows also require catalog management access.

articles.title: Rooms and reservations
articles.summary: The Rooms workspace shows room status, room types, rate plans and reservations.
steps: Review the room and reservation dates.
systemHandles: The API checks availability and the requested room lifecycle transition.
commonMistakes: Do not promise a room that is blocked by an overlapping reservation or active maintenance state.
articles.body:
Section: Property
Roles: Admin, Manager, Front Desk
Permission: rooms.view, rooms.manage, rooms.operate
Screen: rooms
Keywords: rooms, reservations, rate plan, availability

## Overview

The Rooms workspace shows room status, room types, rate plans and reservations.

## Procedure

1. Review the room and reservation dates.
2. Confirm the guest, room type and rate plan.
3. Save or update the reservation using the available action.
4. Use Front Desk for arrival, stay and checkout actions.

## What ServOS handles

The API checks availability and the requested room lifecycle transition.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not promise a room that is blocked by an overlapping reservation or active maintenance state.

articles.title: Front desk
articles.summary: Front Desk supports the guest's arrival, stay and checkout workflows.
steps: Find the reservation and verify the guest and dates.
systemHandles: The API validates the reservation and records the stay and folio transitions.
commonMistakes: Do not check in an unverified guest or release an unfinished maintenance block.
articles.body:
Section: Property
Roles: Admin, Manager, Front Desk
Permission: rooms.view, rooms.operate, folio.view
Screen: frontdesk
Keywords: arrivals, check-in, stay, checkout, folio

## Overview

Front Desk supports the guest's arrival, stay and checkout workflows.

## Procedure

1. Find the reservation and verify the guest and dates.
2. Review room readiness and any maintenance block.
3. Confirm check-in or room move only after the guest and room are verified.
4. Review folio entries and outstanding balance before checkout.

## What ServOS handles

The API validates the reservation and records the stay and folio transitions.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not check in an unverified guest or release an unfinished maintenance block.

articles.title: Housekeeping
articles.summary: Housekeeping updates room readiness as work is completed.
steps: Open the assigned room and review its current readiness state.
systemHandles: The API validates the room status transition and updates the workspace projection.
commonMistakes: Do not mark a room ready before the physical check is complete. Record maintenance instead of hiding an unresolved defect.
articles.body:
Section: Property
Roles: Admin, Manager, Housekeeper
Permission: rooms.view, rooms.operate
Screen: housekeeping
Keywords: housekeeping, room readiness, cleaning

## Overview

Housekeeping updates room readiness as work is completed.

## Procedure

1. Open the assigned room and review its current readiness state.
2. Complete the physical room task.
3. Record the next valid readiness transition.
4. Report damage or maintenance work through the maintenance workflow.

## What ServOS handles

The API validates the room status transition and updates the workspace projection.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not mark a room ready before the physical check is complete. Record maintenance instead of hiding an unresolved defect.

articles.title: Assets and maintenance
articles.summary: The asset register tracks permanent asset identity, location, custody and lifecycle. Maintenance records work orders and parts.
steps: Search by the permanent asset tag.
systemHandles: The API records asset events and work-order changes separately from stock movements.
commonMistakes: Do not use asset edits to erase a transfer or dispose of an item. Record its lifecycle action.
articles.body:
Section: Property
Roles: Admin, Manager, Maintenance
Permission: assets.view, assets.manage, maintenance.view, maintenance.manage
Screen: finance
Keywords: assets, maintenance, custody, work order

## Overview

The asset register tracks permanent asset identity, location, custody and lifecycle. Maintenance records work orders and parts.

## Procedure

1. Search by the permanent asset tag.
2. Record custody or a location transfer with a reason.
3. Open a maintenance work order and assign the work.
4. Record completion only after the work is verified.

## What ServOS handles

The API records asset events and work-order changes separately from stock movements.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not use asset edits to erase a transfer or dispose of an item. Record its lifecycle action.

articles.title: Customer credit
articles.summary: Customer credit is a receivable ledger, separate from cash tender.
steps: Select the customer account and review its status and limit.
systemHandles: The API records each ledger entry, settlement allocation and reconciliation event.
commonMistakes: Do not count a credit charge as cash received or change an old balance directly. Resolve it through the ledger workflow.
articles.body:
Section: Finance
Roles: Admin, Manager, Accountant
Permission: credit.view, credit.charge, credit.settle
Screen: finance
Keywords: customer credit, charge, settlement, balance

## Overview

Customer credit is a receivable ledger, separate from cash tender.

## Procedure

1. Select the customer account and review its status and limit.
2. Record a credit charge only when the sale is approved for credit.
3. For a settlement, select the tender received and review its allocation.
4. Review discrepancies in the reconciliation workflow.

## What ServOS handles

The API records each ledger entry, settlement allocation and reconciliation event.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not count a credit charge as cash received or change an old balance directly. Resolve it through the ledger workflow.

articles.title: Finance and assets
articles.summary: Finance reports and journals summarize committed API events. Asset records use their own lifecycle.
steps: Select a business date or reporting period.
systemHandles: The API builds reports from committed records and restricts them by permission.
commonMistakes: Do not edit a journal total to force a report to balance. Correct the source transaction and regenerate the report.
articles.body:
Section: Finance
Roles: Admin, Manager, Accountant
Permission: accounting.view, reports.view, assets.view
Screen: finance
Keywords: finance, journals, reports, fixed assets

## Overview

Finance reports and journals summarize committed API events. Asset records use their own lifecycle.

## Procedure

1. Select a business date or reporting period.
2. Review the source references behind each total.
3. Reconcile discrepancies using the relevant source workflow.
4. Review asset tags, custody and maintenance records separately from inventory stock.

## What ServOS handles

The API builds reports from committed records and restricts them by permission.

## Common mistakes and correction

Do not edit a journal total to force a report to balance. Correct the source transaction and regenerate the report.
